newsitem.title: UK: West warns Bosnian leaders to stick to peace terms.
newsitem.headline: West warns Bosnian leaders to stick to peace terms.

text.p: An international conference on implementing peace in Bosnia ended on Thursday with a warning to Bosnian leaders that future aid depends on their full compliance with a year-old peace pact.

The conference also agreed to give more support to the international war crimes tribunal at the Hague, including extra resources, and issued a renewed commitment to the Bosnian reconstruction programme, the British Foreign Office said.
In turn, the Bosnian leaders agreed to take "urgent practical steps" to ensure full freedom of movement of people, services and capital across the country.
The two-day talks, grouping more than 50 nations, were called to assess progress on the Bosnian peace deal clinched in the United States a year ago.

"The conference agreed on a set of specific conclusions, placing clear obligations on the parties and setting out the extent of the support the international community is ready to continue to provide," the Foreign Office document said.
Frustration over repeated delays in implementing the civilian aspects of the so-called Dayton agreement has led Western leaders to link aid to a renewed commitment to genuine peace on the ground.
Overseas Development Minister Baroness Chalker said it was vital that international aid was conditional on the Bosnian authorities taking full responsibility for their own future.
"Conditionality is not blackmail," she told the meeting.
Among the most contentious issues yet to be resolved is the fate of indicted war criminals, the vast majority of whom remain at large despite widespread evidence of crimes against humanity.

Delegates agreed that the Hague tribunal should be better equipped in its investigations but a top European Union official expressed doubt that authorities in the former Yugoslavia were ready to comply with the West's calls for greater cooperation.
EU External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said he was not convinced Bosnian authorities would comply and that the international community must force them by "whatever means".
Britain, however, has expressed grave doubts about using peacekeepers to round up the indicted men, fearing casualties as it seeks to make its exit from Bosnia in the months ahead.
